chunks: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah from Abu Ja'far from Ali ibn Hadid and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abd Allah from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him, 'A man forgets the first Takbir of the opening.' He said, 'If he remembers it before bowing, he says the Takbir, then recites, then bows. And if he remembers it during the prayer, he says it while standing in the place of the Takbir, before the recitation and after the recitation.' I said, 'And if he remembers it after the prayer?' He said, 'Let him make it up, and there is no penalty upon him.'

His saying (peace be upon him) 'Let him make it up' means the prayer, and he did not mean the Takbir alone. As for his saying 'and there is no penalty upon him,' it means from punishment, because he did not intentionally leave it, but merely forgot. So when he repeats the prayer, there is nothing upon him.

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرَةِ الْاِفْتِتَاحِ: The initial Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar') at the start of prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they forget the opening Takbir during prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of nasa (forgetfulness) regarding the opening Takbir, distinguishing between correcting the error within the prayer structure versus requiring a full qada (make-up) if remembered after completion. The Imam specifies that 'qada' refers to repeating the entire prayer rather than merely the Takbir, emphasizing that unintentional omission incurs no sin (la shay' 'alayhi), reflecting the Shia principle of ease in ritual purity and prayer validity.
